findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - A Windows user named José installs Git with Scoop under their profile and runs the tests with Python 3.11 using the Windows cp1252 code page.
Git reports its executable path in UTF-8, but `text=True` decodes it using Python's locale encoding. The profile name is therefore garbled, so the ancestor search misses the installed Bash and skips test_9 despite Bash being available. The shared-history rule remains unchecked on that Scoop setup. Read Git's output as UTF-8. See [Git's Windows path conversion](https://github.com/git/git/blob/master/exec-cmd.c#L172-L186) and the [Python subprocess documentation](https://docs.python.org/3.11/library/subprocess.html).
findings.title: Gate: test_9 skips when Git for Windows is installed through Scoop

stop.reason: Owner chose on 21 Nov 2026: one more round for the UTF-8 path finding and the missing platform markers

why: The v1.2.45 release check fails on Windows in two places. First, forge merge run from inside the fix's worktree merges, cannot remove the worktree, then fails with 'git branch failed: not a git repository' (tests/test_merge_refreshes_behind_base.py test_2, all four cases; it passed on v1.2.44). Second, tests/test_record_only_failed_results.py test_9 runs a workflow step with bash, which on the Windows runner is the uninstalled WSL bash.
